# Who promotes partners

<!-- Generated by scripts/partner-programs.mjs from data/partner-programs.json, data/partner-programs-ai.json, data/partner-programs-motion.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Most partner programs list you. Some also **promote** you: a co-marketing campaign, a post on their social accounts, a feature on their blog, a case study, a newsletter slot, a featured placement, a speaking slot, a podcast, a joint press release, or a partner badge. This page pulls those programs out of every sector tracker so an application can be chosen for the audience it buys, not just the listing.

**99 open programs offer promotion** across [Big tech](./big-tech-programs.md), [AI](./ai-programs.md), [Motion](./motion-programs.md). A tag is set only where the program states the benefit or has a documented record of doing it for partners; the note says which, and how to ask.

```sh
npm run programs:promo                    # the best single asks, across sectors
npm run programs:promo -- blog            # every program that will publish a blog post about us
npm run programs -- --benefit <id> --name "Blog post" --state received --note "<url>"   # record a promotion we won
```

## Keeping it true

- **Tag only what is stated or documented.** A company having a social account is not a promotion benefit. Mark a track-record-only tag as such in `promo_note`.
- **Ask on the way in.** Put the promotion ask in the application or acceptance reply; most programs grant it at onboarding and rarely later.
- **Record what we win.** A published post, case study, or spotlight is a benefit: record it with `--benefit` and the live URL in `--note`, then add it to [press-kit.md](../press-kit.md) coverage where it belongs.
- **$THREE is the only coin we promote.** A crypto ecosystem promoting three.ws is welcome; three.ws promoting another token in return is not part of any deal without owner approval.
